text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Social policy experts in ruling Christian Democrats (CDU/CSU) largely united behind Labour Minister Norbert Bluem's pension reform plans.
- Kurt Biedenkopf, state premier of Saxony, says postponement of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) would not endanger European integration.
- Future of telecommunications alliance between Cable and Wireless , Veba and RWE in doubt.
- Auditors criticise Transport Ministry.
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel emphasises need for truly independent central bank.
HANDELSBLATT
- Free Democrats (FDP), junior partners in ruling coalition, speak out against higher oil tax.
- President of the German Trade and Industry Association (DIHT) says only countries taking part in EMU will reap its benefits.
- Men's fashion industry optimistic about future, hoping for 3.6 percent increase in turnover in 1997.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- FDP, rejecting Bluem's pension plans, wants new commission to look at the issue.
- Health Minister Horst Seehofer criticises European Commission's role in mad cow disease scare.
- Federal Labour Office president says January unemployment reached highest level in Germany's postwar history.
- European Commission set to take action against Deutsche Post AG for suppressing market forces, rival says.
DIE WELT
- FDP steps up criticism of Bleum and his pension plans.
- State premiers call for new round of talks involving employers, trade unions and politicians to discuss unemployment.
- Institute of German Economy (IW) says tax reform plans will only give business minimal reduction of tax burden.
- Space industry criticises Technology Minister Juergen Ruettgers for not including them in talks about new research in their sector.
